info.description:
Web Service specifications for interaction between Ohris data and third party applications.

It requires the creation of an API account from the Ohris administration interface. Authentication has type **http/basic** and must be integrated into each request.
# 1. Functional area
Ohris's API resources are grouped by functional domain (**Absence**, **Activity**, ...).
All of them use some shared bases resources united in a specific domain called **Common**:
  https://[host]/api/v2/common/users.json?sort=last_name:desc,first_name:asc

![Functional domains diagram](./assets/img/api-doc-resources-diagram.png)

## Usable and upcoming API functionalities:

- **Common**:
    Basic data common to each Ohris module.
    - `Structures`: services organization under one or more companies
    - `Users`: basic user information as name, email address or department
    - `Groups`: access configuration logic for users (functional axis and structures perimeter)
    - `Contracts` and `StatusType`: categories allowing users discrimination
    - `WorkCycles` and `WorkCycleAssignment` : configuration and assignments of worked periods
    - `Profiles`: configuration about accounts permissions
    - `BankHolidays` and `BankHolidaysAssignment`: bank holidays calendars configuration and assignments of these calendars to users

- **Absence**:
    Leaves's configuration and data including teleworking and all kind of absences
    - `AbsenceTypes`: Usable absence type configuration (paid holidays, sick leaves...)
    - `Absences`: absence periods set for each user with status information
    - `HomeOffice`: teleworked periods set for each user with status information
    - `Counters`: credit, consumed and balance of days available individually for an absence type

- **Activity**:
    Activity tracking configuration and data including project reporting
    - `Projets`: Projects/Activities configuration with hierarchical task decomposition
    - `Imputations`: activity duration by days set for each user and each project

- **Time**:
    Clocking in time tracking 
    - `Punches`: adding a clock punch for a user# 2. Return format description

## 2.1 Single items

Each item of a resource has an unique Ohris ID that can be used to get details of this resource.

The details can be directly recovered by `get` method:
```
  https://[host]/api/v2/[domain]/[resource name]/[resource ID].json
```

### Sample:

```
  https://[host]/api/v2/common/users/999.json
```

Will return has JSON:
```
  {
    "id": "999",
    "payroll_id": "9999999Z",
    "email": "arthure.martin@sncf.fr",
    "first_name": "Arthure",
    "last_name": "Martin",
    "department": {
        "id": "75",
        "code": "766931",
        "label": "PERSONNEL COMMUNICATION"
    },
    "enabled": 1
}
```

## 2.2 Collection of items

Search methods always provide a collection structure that permit to return a partial or a complet list of items.

Each collection structure provide information data to help the WS client's manipulations:
- `@context`: Type of the resources provided in `data` node.
- `@id`: URI of the resources provided in `data` node.
- `hydra:member`: List of resources corresponding to the current search.
- `hydra:totalItems`: Total items available in the collection.
- `hydra:view`: Useful links to navigate through the collection
    - `@id`: URI to the current filtered collection at the current offset
    - `hydra:first`: URI to the first page of the current filtered collection
    - `hydra:last`: URI to the last page of the current filtered collection
    - `hydra:next`: URL of the next page relative to the current filtered collection offset
- `hydra:search`: Description of available parameters  for the REST action
    - `hydra:template`: URI template of the current action
    - `hydra:mapping`: Collection of aviable action parameters

Collection can be recovered by `get` method:
```
  https://[host]/api/v2/[domain]/[resource name].json?[filters parameters]&[sort parameters]&[rang parameters]
```

With:

- [filters parameters]: Query filters for the current search. This parameters are specifics for each resource. So please see each resource definition to know which filters can be used and how to use them.
  ```
    https://[host]/api/v2/common/users.json?last_name=glob:Mar*&enabled=true
  ```

- [sort parameters]: You may use the `sort` parameter to get a result sorted by one or more fields values (used semicolons to separat field's names).
  ```
    https://[host]/api/v2/common/users.json?sort=last_name:desc;first_name:asc
  ```

  Add the `desc` or `asc` parameter after  each sorted field name (this sample show how to sort by the last names from A to Z and by first names from Z to A in as same table)

- [rang parameters]: Limit the number of items returned and the offset in the `hydra:member` node.
  - [page]: page number for the range items to get.  The first page is always "1"
  - [limit]: number of items to get in the range (max item returned in `hydra:member` node).

  This gets the first 10 results:
  ```
    https://[host]/api/v2/[domain]/[resource name].json?users?page=1&limit=10
  ```

  This gets the next 10 results:
  ```
    https://[host]/api/v2/[domain]/[resource name].json?page=2&limit=10
  ```

  The result has an auto-limitation to 20 items if the `limit` parameter is not set in the query.

### Sample:

```
  https://[host]/api/v2/common/users.json?last_name=glob:Ma*&enabled=true&sort=last_name:desc;first_name:asc&page=2&limit=5

# 3. Manipulate filters parameters

## 3.1 filters operators

Ohris API use OData keywords to specify how to use given parameters of the request.

Add the operator before the constant value in the filters parameters
```
  https://[host]/api/v2/[domain]/[resource name].json?parameter_name=operator:value&[sort parameters]&[rang parameters]
```

Operators can be cumulated
```
  https://[host]/api/v2/[domain]/[resource name].json?id=gte:42;id:lt:66&[sort parameters]&[rang parameters]
```

### list of filters operators

| keyword | parameter type         | Effect                                                                   |
| --------| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

get.description:
Returns the complete information schema for one absence.

### Period definition

The granularity of an absence period is the half day:
- the period start at a date and a slice indicator to specify if it start since the morning (start_slice=`1`) or since the midday (start_slice=`2`).
- the period end at a date and a slice indicator to specify if it end at the midday (start_slice=`1`) or at the evening (start_slice=`2`).

Samples:

> start_date=2022-11-10&start_slice=1&end_date=2022-11-10&start_slice=2 describe a complete absence on the 10th of november.

> start_date=2022-11-10&start_slice=2&end_date=2022-11-11&start_slice=1 describe an absence on the 10th afternoon and the 11th morning.

### Status of an absence:

| keyword          | Description                                                                                           |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |         
| validated         | The absence period is validated                                                                       |         
| wait_validation   | The absence period must be validated by a manager before get validated                                |       
| wait_cancellation | The absence period was previously validated and the cancellation request must be granted by a manager |        
| canceled          | The absence period has disappeared from plannings and balance calculation                             |

### Time value

The unit of the `day_count` depend of the count_mode set for the absence type (generally in days but it may be in minutes if `count_mode`=`WorkcycleHours`)

Counters are only available for absence types that have the option counter associated checked in the Ohris setting.

post.description:
Create a new sporadic or recurring telework request for a specific user.

Any teleworked day will be automaticaly validated, if the beneficiary activated it, mail to confirm the creation will be send.

Example of body for a sporadic request:
```
[
    'user' => 42,
    'start_date' => '2022-12-21',
    'end_date' => '2022-12-21',
    'start_slice' => 1,
    'end_slice' => 2,
    'periodic_days' => [], # 11 => monday AM, 12 => monday PM... 72 => sunday PM
    'frequency' => 1, # must always be at least 1, even for non-recurring requests
    'location' => null # use the label of a teleworking location of the user or null if you want to use de default location of the user (home)
]
```
- start_slice is 1 to start the morning, 2 to start the afternoon.
- end_slice is 1 to end in the middle of the day, 2 to end in the end of the day.
- periodic_days is an empty table, if filled up it's a recurring request.
- frequency must be 1.
- location is null, it's used to define the default location of the user (home) could not be an empty string.

Example of body for a recurring request:
```
[
    'user' => 42,
    'start_date' => '2023-01-01',
    'end_date' => '2023-12-31',
    'start_slice' => 1,
    'end_slice' => 2,
    'periodic_days' => [11,12,31,32],
    'frequency' => 2,
    'location' => 'maison de campagne'
]
```
- periodic days works with half days, even it's not permitted in company settings.
- 11 is for monday AM, 12 monday PM... 72 for sunday PM.
- Frequency 2 means days will be filed every other week, starting on start_date week.
- Location 'maison de campagne' must be already created and validated before to be used.

Post action could not be used to update an existing request.

get.description:
Returns the complete information schema for one teleworked period.

The HomeOffices resource refers to a period (start_date to end_date). But there is two cases of setting:

### 1) "periodic_days" is empty: the period is fully teleworked

As same as the Absence resource, there may have some days-off, absences or cancelled teleworked days in the period so becarfull about using this data to report teleworked days (HomeOfficeEvents may be a better choice for that).

Note: `frequency` value has no use in this case.

### 2) "periodic_days" is not empty: the period is punctually teleworked with a notion of recurrence.

`periodic_days` give numeric codes to show the pattern of teleworked days in a week: the first digit is the day number of the week (1=Monday, 7=Sunday) and the second is the day slice (1=morning, 2=afternoon)

Sample: `periodic_days=[11,12,31]` refer to weeks where Monday is fully teleworked and Wednesday is teleworked only on morning.

frequency value set the recurrence of the week pattern: `frequency=1` means that every weeks get the pattern. `frequency=2` means that pattern is set every tow weeks (starting on start_date period).

### Meaning of others attributes  :

- `start_slice` is 1 if the period start on morning at start_date, 2 to start the afternoon.
- `end_slice` is 1 if the end in the middle of the day at end_date, 2 to end in the end of the day.
- `location` is linked to the  HomeOfficeLocations resource. The null value it's used to define the default location of the user.

### Notice  :

- `created_datetime` and `logs.datetime` are given as Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

get.description:
Returns a collection of structures.

Companies and departments are hierarchised in **structures** trees. Each company has his own tree with his departments (and potentials sub-departments).

Each tree node has an `id`, a `parent_id`, and a `root_id`.

![structure tree parameters](./assets/img/api-doc-structure.png)

Compagnies nodes always has a `parent_id` set to **null**. So we can get all compagnies with:
```
https://[host]/api/v2/common/structures.json?parent_id=null
```

`root_id` is the `id` of the company. So we can get all departments linked to a specifique company (using his id):
```
https://[host]/api/v2/common/structures.json?root_id=[id of the company node]
```

The tree hierarchy can be recompiled by linking nodes with the `parent_id` value (you have to set this logic on your side).

The user is created with inactive status to prevent authentication with a non functional account. No module is activated (remember that billing is done on accounts that have active modules). It's important to link the user to a last node of the structure tree (assigning the user to a intermediate node or  directly to a company may cause functional issues in the application). Please see the Common/Structures ressource documentation to get more information.

post.description:
Creates a new work cycle model with its schedule grid.

The grid is given through **slices**: two per day (morning then afternoon), so 14 slices for a
weekly model, 28 for a model repeated every two weeks, and so on. A `duration` of "0" marks a
half-day that is not worked.

```json
{
    "rate": 0.8,
    "time_base": 2100,
    "date": "2024-01-01",
    "structures": ["/api/v2/common/structures/1"],
    "slices": [
        {"day_number": 1, "slice_position": 1, "duration": 210},
        {"day_number": 1, "slice_position": 2, "duration": 210},
        {"day_number": 3, "slice_position": 1, "duration": 0},
        {"day_number": 3, "slice_position": 2, "duration": 0}
    ]
}
```

Leave `label` out and it is generated from the rate, the time base and the grid — and kept in
sync with them afterwards. Provide one and it is used as is, and no longer recomputed.

The triplet label / rate / time_base must be unique.

Post action cannot be used to update an existing work cycle model. To update one, use the PATCH method instead.

slices.description: The schedule grid, two slices per day

structures.description: IRIs of the companies allowed to use this model

time_base.description: Minutes worked for a full-time equivalent

get.description:
A work cycle model describe the theoretical time worked for each day in a week.
Each day is splited in tow **slices** section. You may get 14 slices to describe a model repeatable each week:
- day_number=1 and slice_position=1 describe the Monday morning
- day_number=1 and slice_position=2 describe the Monday afternoon
- ...
- day_number=7 and slice_position=2 describe the Sunday afternoon

Note that some models give 28 slices or more because there periodicity is repeatable every X weeks.

The attribute **duration** of each slice give the theoretical worked time for the half-day:
- the period is not worked if **duration** is set to "0"
- the theoretical worked time is given in minutes if **duration** is an integer (a value of "210" is equivalent to 3 hours and 30 minutes)

Partially updates an existing work cycle model.

As intended by the standard PATCH operation: there is no need to specify the complete set of data.
Give only the data to change in the targeted ressource.

Beware that **slices** behave as a whole: the grid you send replaces the previous one entirely,
so send every slice of the model, not only those that change.

A model whose label was generated sees it recomputed whenever the rate, the time base or the grid
changes. A model with a label of its own keeps it.

Patch action cannot be used to create a work cycle model. To create one, use the POST method instead.
